title: The Rising Vault
story: Deep beneath the drowned cathedral, Ondrivale the Sump Warden unplugs the floor and lets the black water climb, laughing that it always wins the race. Two lamp-keepers are stranded on a stone ledge 63 inches above the waterline. Mr 6 slaps his siphon-shell onto the wall and starts pumping while he does the math in his head.
question: The water rises 12 inches every minute, and Mr 6's siphon pulls out 7.5 inches every minute. How many minutes until the water reaches the ledge?
solution: The water really gains only 12 - 7.5 = 4.5 inches each minute.
The ledge is 63 inches up, so 63 / 4.5 = 14 minutes.
Mr 6 has 14 minutes to get the lamp-keepers out.
praise: Dividing by a rise-rate was exactly the right instinct — the missing step was subtracting the siphon first, so the water only truly climbs 4.5 inches a minute.
hint: The water rises AND the siphon drains at the same time. Find the net rise for one minute before you divide.
victory: Mr 6 walks the keepers up the stair with four whole minutes to spare, and Ondrivale, out-pumped and out-thought, gurgles down its own drain in a huff.
imagePrompt: A brave numeral-six knight with a blue cape bracing a spiral siphon-shell against a flooded cathedral crypt wall while a bloated water-warden sneers from the dark rising pool, lantern light glinting off the surface.
